goal: One intermediate representation for every hex body ClamAV, YARA and Guardian rules can express, so atom selection, the verify VM and the compiler share a single model of a subsignature.
scope: src/compile/ir.zig: Subsig { parts, mods, target, offset } where a part is a list of ops LIT, MASKED (value/mask byte pairs for ?a, a? and ??), ALT, NALT (!(..)), GAPF (fixed {n}) and a PART_END carrying the min/max window for {n-m}, {-n}, {n-}, * and [n-m]
Modifiers nocase, wide, ascii, fullword (::i ::w ::a ::f) and boundary anchors (B) and (L)

Compile-time expansion: wide becomes 00-interleaved literals; small fixed-width alternations expand into literal variants; nocase expands to at most 16 variants and otherwise marks the subsig for a folded partition
Hex body tokenizer with precise error positions for every rejected construct
Every rejection is recorded in the coverage report with a reason code
out_of_scope: Offsets and target types in .ndb lines (P4.02)
notes: The IR is the contract between the compiler and src/match/verify_vm.zig: keep ops small and fixed-size so programs serialise into the SUBSIG_PROG section with u32 offsets
Reproduce ClamAV semantics exactly: each {n-m} part matches independently, * spans the whole remaining input, ::f uses ClamAV's word-boundary definition
accept: Round-trip test: parse then print reproduces every body in the E0 census set, modulo whitespace
Fuzz target for the tokenizer runs 10M iterations without a crash or unbounded allocation
Every grammar feature in the ClamAV body format doc has a unit test

goal: Parse .ndb extended signatures, including every offset form and target type, into the IR so they can be partitioned by file type and anchored where possible.
scope: src/compile/parse_ndb.zig: Name:TargetType:Offset:HexSignature[:min_flevel[:max_flevel]]
Offset kinds: * (any), absolute n, EP+n / EP-n, EOF-n, Sx+n (section-relative), SL+n, SE (section end), VI, and the n,maxshift form
Target types 0 to 14 mapped to partitions (any, PE, OLE2, normalised HTML, mail, graphics, ELF, normalised ASCII, Mach-O, PDF, flash, java, and the internal ones)
Functionality-level filtering against the engine's declared level, recorded in the coverage report
.ign2 drops applied at compile time
out_of_scope: Evaluating offsets at scan time (P4.06, P4.07)
notes: Store offset kind as off_kind u8, off_a i32, off_shift u32 in the subsig program header so anchored lookups need no reparsing
Unknown target types are rejected with a reason, never silently mapped to type 0
accept: Parses every line of the current daily and main .ndb files, with rejections fully accounted for in the coverage report
Unit tests for each offset kind and the maxshift form
Counts per target type match the E0 census

goal: Choose, for every subsignature, the rarest 4-byte window as its atom, using a 4-gram frequency model built from a benign corpus, and classify it into tiers A to D. Candidate rate, not signature count, decides scan speed.
scope: Offline tool that builds the 4-gram frequency model from the benign corpus manifest and ships it with the compiler

src/compile/atoms.zig: enumerate fixed runs of 4 or more bytes and bounded expansions of small ALT/MASKED groups; score by estimated benign frequency; penalise 00, FF, CC and 90 runs, padding, common prologues and MZ/PE headers
Tiers by the rarest fixed run length L: A (L >= 11, stride 8), B (7 to 10, stride 4), C (4 to 6, stride 1), D (L <= 3)
Per-subsig record of atom bytes, gram offset inside the anchor, and tier
Histogram output feeding E3
notes: ClamAV's Aho-Corasick uses a 2 to 3 byte prefix depth, which is why its candidate rate is high; rare atoms are the main lever
A sampled stride s is safe only when every sampled position lands inside the anchor: insert all s 4-grams at offsets 0..s-1 of the anchor
[E] target: at least 10x fewer candidates per MB than prefix selection on the benign corpus
accept: Every in-scope subsig gets an atom or an explicit tier-D classification
Tier histogram for the full database is written to the coverage report
Deterministic output: the same inputs produce a byte-identical atom table

goal: Serialise per-partition split-block Bloom prefilters and atom hash tables into the hot region of the .zavdb, so the daemon maps them clean and never builds them at runtime.
scope: PREFILTER[p] section: 64-byte header (q=4, stride, sbbf_blocks_log2, hash_seed, short filter offset) followed by 2^B blocks of 32 bytes (8 u32 words), plus a separate smaller SBBF for tier C
ATOM_TABLE[p]: linear probing at 50% load, 8-byte slots {atom u32, first u32} pointing at 8-byte entries {subsig u24, gram_off u8, flags u16, anchor_len u8}
Each partition k >= 1 includes type-0 atoms so each stream is scanned once
Sizing for about 16 bits per key, 32-byte blocks aligned to 64
Reuse the SBBF builder from zig-regex literals instead of a second copy
notes: Expected false-positive rate about 0.1 to 0.3% at 16 bits per key; confirm in E2
Type-0 duplication costs a few MB of clean file pages [E]; record the real number
All offsets are u32 relative to their section; nothing is relocated at load
accept: Compile the full database; per-partition filter sizes and load factors are printed by zav info
Every atom inserted is found by a reference scalar probe (no false negatives) in a property test
Measured false-positive rate on random data within 2x of the theoretical value

goal: The stage-one scan loop: sampled 4-byte probes into the partition's SBBF with no loop-carried dependency, SIMD hashing of 16 positions at once, and a branch-free candidate ring.
scope: Per position: a = load_u32(p+i); h = (a ^ seed) * K64; block = h >> (64 - B); 8 bit positions from h times 8 odd constants; test all 8 words with one vptest (AVX2) or cmtst plus umaxv (NEON)
Vectorise the hashing (one 32-byte load, comptime @shuffle masks, @Vector(16,u32) multiply); keep probes scalar
Branch-free append into a 4096-entry u32 candidate ring, drained when full or at the end of each 64 KiB sub-block
Stage two: prefetch ATOM_TABLE slots for the next 8 candidates, then a u64-masked anchor compare
Kernels built per CPU variant (x86-64-v2, v3, aarch64) and selected at runtime
notes: No gathers: Intel parts with the GDS mitigation make them slow
[E] per-byte cost: tier A about 0.6 cycles, tier B about 1.2, tier C about 4.5; PE partition with A and B only about 2 cycles per byte, roughly 2 GB/s per core
Zig has no runtime-index byte shuffle builtin; use inline asm (vpshufb / tbl) where a runtime shuffle is needed
accept: Scalar reference and SIMD kernels return identical candidate sets on 1 GB of random and benign input
Micro-benchmark per tier recorded for x86_64 and aarch64 in bench results
Zero allocations inside the loop, asserted by a counting allocator

goal: A small verify VM that confirms a candidate against the full subsignature, searching parts outward from the anchor within their gap windows, with hard step budgets so no input can make it slow.
scope: Executes SUBSIG_PROG: LIT, MASKED, ALT, NALT, GAPF, PART_END min/max, BOUND
Start at the anchor part; search earlier parts backwards and later parts forwards inside [min,max], using SIMD memchr on the rarest byte then a masked compare
Backtracking over candidate positions with a per-subsig step budget (default 4096) and a per-file verify budget
Budget exhaustion records limit metadata on the result (Heuristics.Limits.Exceeded style), never a silent pass
Offset-kind checks (ABS, EP, EOF, section) evaluated against the file context before running the program
notes: Reproduce exactly: * across the whole file, independent {n-m} parts, the maxshift window, the ::f boundary rule, and count and offset ordering rules
Programs are read straight from the mapped blob; the VM keeps state in the worker scratch only
accept: Matches libclamav on a synthetic signature per grammar feature (checked with sigtool --test-sigs)
Adversarial inputs never exceed the configured budget, and the limit flag is set when they hit it
Fuzz target over random programs and inputs runs clean for 10M iterations

goal: Signatures pinned to a fixed offset (EP+n, EOF-n, Sx+n, absolute) are checked with a direct lookup at that offset instead of being scanned for.
scope: ANCHORED_INDEX[p]: groups by (off_kind, off_a); each group is a small hash table keyed by the 4 bytes at that offset, mapping to subsig lists
Groups with non-zero off_shift get a short window scan of off_shift plus length bytes
Runs once per file after format parsing provides EP, sections and size
Signatures that are anchored skip the stream prefilter entirely
out_of_scope: PE and ELF parsing that supplies EP and sections (P5.05, P5.06)
notes: Cost is one lookup per distinct group present in the partition, independent of signature count
Anchored tier-D subsigs are handled here rather than by the 2 to 3 byte gram bitmaps
Until P5.05 and P5.06 land, test with synthetic entry points and sections; the real PE and ELF sample differential checks run in the P5.20 gate.
accept: Every anchored signature in the database is reachable through the index (compile-time check)
Differential test against libclamav on PE and ELF samples with EP and section-relative signatures
Benchmark shows anchored lookups add under 2 microseconds per file [E]

goal: Parse .ldb logical signatures: subsignatures, the target description block, and logical expressions compiled to a compact RPN program.
scope: src/compile/parse_ldb.zig: SignatureName;TargetDescriptionBlock;LogicalExpression;Subsig0;Subsig1;...
TDB predicates: Engine, Target, FileSize, EntryPoint, NumberOfSections, Container, Intermediates, IconGroup (rejected with reason until icons ship)
Expressions to RPN ops: HIT i, COUNT i, CMP EQ/GT/LT k, AND, OR, DISTINCT_GE k for =X,Y, OFFSETS i for multi-offset conditions
LDB_TABLE: 32-byte header per signature {sig, nsub, expr_off, tdb_off, flags}
PCRE and byte-compare subsigs are parsed here and handed to their own issues
notes: ClamAV allows at most 64 subsignatures per logical signature: enforce it
Subsignature modifiers and offsets reuse the P4.01 IR and P4.02 offset parsing
accept: Parses every .ldb line in current main and daily, rejections accounted for
RPN evaluation unit tests for every expression form, including nested counts and distinct counts
Fuzz target for the expression parser runs clean

goal: Track logical-signature state per file at a cost proportional to what was touched, and evaluate only the logical signatures that saw a hit.
scope: Per-worker open-addressing table of 8192 slots x 16 bytes {ldb u32, mask u64, cnt_off u16, dead u8}, reset through a touched list
Count side arena of u16 counters for subsigs used in count conditions
On first touch: evaluate TDB predicates against the file context; mark dead when they fail
Overflow spills to the arena: slower, never a failure
Finalize: evaluate RPN for touched, live signatures; report the first match or all matches in ALLMATCH mode
notes: A dense bitset over about 400k subsigs would cost 50 KB to clear per file and a stamp array 2.4 MB per thread; the sparse table avoids both
128 KB per worker counts toward the private-dirty budget in the design's memory table
accept: Differential tests against libclamav on logical signatures with counts, distinct counts and offsets
Per-file reset cost measured as O(touched): flat when the database grows
No allocation in the hot path, asserted in tests

goal: Short subsignatures (tier D, 3 bytes or fewer) do not get their own stream prefilter when the logical expression cannot be true without a longer partner: they are checked only after that partner hits.
scope: Compile-time required-subsig analysis over each RPN expression: find subsigs whose hit is necessary for the expression to be true
Mark tier-D subsigs deferred when a required partner is tier A to C
Second pass in finalize scans only deferred subsigs of logical signatures whose partner hit
Remaining tier-D subsigs fall back to anchored lookups or 2 to 3 byte gram bitmaps with positional checks
Coverage report counts deferred, anchored and bitmap tier-D subsigs
notes: This is the same idea as Hyperscan's Rose decomposition
[E] target: at least 90% of tier-D subsigs deferrable or anchorable
accept: No detection changes against the non-deferred path on the malware corpus (differential test)
Candidate rate per MB drops on the benign corpus, recorded in bench results

goal: PCRE subsignatures in .ldb run through zig-regex byte mode, only when their trigger expression is true and only over their offset window.
scope: src/match/regex_bridge.zig: compile ClamAV PCRE subsigs with zig-regex bytes mode and its flags (i, s, m, x, and the ClamAV-specific g, r, e)
Trigger evaluation over other subsig hits before running the regex
Matcher with caller-supplied scratch, a capped DFA state count and a step budget
Bounded process-wide read-mostly cache of compiled programs (about 4 MB) until serialised programs live in the blob
Unsupported constructs rejected at compile time with reasons in the coverage report
notes: zig-regex today maps \xHH to UTF-8 code points; byte mode from P2.01 is required
Required literal factors from P2.04 feed atom selection for regex-only subsigs
accept: Differential test against libclamav on every PCRE subsig in the database that compiles
Worst-case regex inputs respect the step budget
Cache stays under its cap under the full database and the malware corpus

goal: Support ClamAV byte-compare subsignatures, which read a number at an offset relative to another subsig hit and compare it.
scope: Parse (subsig#offset#options#comparisons) forms: hex, decimal and automatic encodings, little and big endian, byte widths 1 to 8
Comparison operators <, >, = with up to two comparisons
Evaluate after the referenced subsig's offsets are known, inside finalize
Bounds checks against the file size, with a limit flag on violation
notes: Byte compare reads only a few bytes; keep it in the logical-evaluation path, not the stream loop
accept: Unit tests for every encoding, width and endianness
Differential test against libclamav on the byte-compare signatures in the database

goal: File-type magic (.ftm) decides the partition and embedded-type triggers for each file, and container signatures (.cdb) match on archive member metadata.
scope: src/compile/parse_ftm.zig and an FTM_TRIE section in the hot region: magic at fixed offsets plus the embedded-type entries
src/fmt/ftm.zig: classify from the first 4 KiB; return type plus embedded-type triggers
src/compile/parse_cdb.zig and a CDB_TABLE: container type, sizes, encryption flag, position, filename regex
Member iteration hook that evaluates .cdb once per member, with the filename regex through zig-regex
notes: Type detection must match libclamav so that target-type partitions see the same files
Embedded-type triggers (for example a PE inside a document) feed the container framework
accept: File-type classification matches clamscan --debug on a mixed corpus of at least 10k files
Every .cdb signature in the database compiles or is rejected with a reason
Unit tests for overlapping magic entries

goal: Compile the YARA subset ClamAV supports (text, hex and regex strings with string-driven conditions, no modules) into the same IR and logical RPN, so YARA rules cost the same as native signatures.
scope: src/compile/yara/: lexer, parser, semantic checks
Strings: text with nocase, wide, ascii, fullword, xor over a small range (expanded); hex strings mapped onto the hex IR; regex strings through zig-regex bytes with atoms from required literal factors
Conditions: and, or, not, #a op n, $a at N, $a in (a..b), N of (...), any/all of them, filesize, uint8/16/32[be](off), @a[i]
Lowered onto the logical RPN, extended with offset predicates
Rules using modules, import, global or external variables are rejected and logged in the coverage report
notes: Limits match ClamAV: at most 64 strings per rule, wildcard-separated segments at least 2 bytes
accept: A public YARA rule set compiles with every rejection explained
Differential tests against yara and libclamav on supported rules and a sample corpus
Fuzz target for the YARA parser runs clean

goal: Guardian's own rule format is the YARA subset plus a TOML metadata file, compiled into the same database, with a starter rule pack for threats ClamAV covers poorly in our ecosystem.
scope: Rule pack layout: rules/<family>/*.yar plus rules/<family>/meta.toml (category, severity, references, false-positive notes, owner)
Compiler support: a source tag guardian in SIGMETA, names prefixed Guardian.
Starter pack: web shells (PHP, JSP, ASPX), JavaScript skimmers, malicious npm install scripts, cryptominer droppers, Linux backdoors from public reports
Signed rule-pack bundle format for distribution by the Guardian app
Test fixtures: one benign and one matching sample per rule (synthetic where samples cannot be published)
notes: No new language: anything a rule needs beyond the subset is a YARA subset gap to fix in P4.14
accept: zav compile accepts the pack; zav coverage lists every rule
Each rule matches its fixture and does not fire on the benign corpus
Bundle signature verification rejects a tampered pack

goal: Pick the stage-one prefilter with measurements, not argument: split-block Bloom with tiers, an FDR-style shift-or, a depth-4 double-array Aho-Corasick and Teddy, on the real atom set.
scope: Benchmark program over the B1 benign and B2 large-file corpora with the full compiled atom set
Metrics: GB/s per core including stage two, candidates per MB, cache misses, SMT on and off
Variants: SBBF tiers A to C, FDR prototype, double-array AC depth 4, Teddy for small partitions
Results committed to docs/experiments/E2.md and the chosen design recorded in DESIGN.md
notes: Pass line: SBBF on the PE partition at least 1 GB/s per core including stage two, and at least 3x clamd raw throughput
If it fails: build the FDR variant or split partitions further
accept: Results for x86_64 and aarch64 are committed with hardware details
A decision is recorded and the losing variants are removed or kept behind a build flag with a reason

goal: Measure what rare-atom selection and tier-D deferral actually buy compared with prefix selection.
scope: Compile the database twice: frequency-model atoms against 3-byte prefixes
Measure candidates per MB and verify steps per MB on B1 and B2
Report tier-D counts: deferred, anchored, bitmap
Write docs/experiments/E3.md
notes: Pass line: at least 10x fewer candidates than prefix selection; at least 90% of tier-D subsigs deferrable or anchorable
If it fails: per-signature hints in the compiler, or accept a slower partition and document it
accept: Numbers committed and the [E] figures in DESIGN.md replaced
Follow-up issues opened for any partition that misses the pass line

goal: Prove the verify VM cannot be driven into slow paths by crafted input, with the full database loaded.
scope: Build worst-case inputs against the real database: maximal candidate density, long unbounded parts, many alternations
Measure ms per MB and steps per MB per input
Verify budgets trigger and set the limit flag
Write docs/experiments/E4.md and add the inputs to the adversarial corpus
notes: Pass line: no input exceeds 50 ms per MB
accept: All A1 inputs stay under the pass line in CI
Budget values in the default config are justified by the measurements

goal: Confirm zig-regex byte mode gives the same answers as PCRE2 on every ClamAV PCRE subsignature and YARA regex string we accept.
scope: Harness that runs each accepted pattern through zig-regex bytes and PCRE2 on the benign and malware corpora
Report compile failures, result differences and timing
Write docs/experiments/E13.md
notes: Pass line: at least 99% of patterns compile with identical results; the rest are marked unsupported in the coverage report
PCRE2 is used only by this harness, never linked into the engine
accept: Results committed; each difference is either fixed upstream or listed as unsupported with a reason

goal: A differential test suite that checks zav against libclamav for every signature grammar feature, so semantic drift is caught on every change.
scope: Synthetic signature and matching or non-matching sample per grammar feature (hex ops, offsets, modifiers, logical forms, counts, PCRE flags, byte compare, ftm, cdb)
Runner that compares zav verdicts and names with clamscan using the same database built by sigtool
CI job (Linux) with ClamAV installed only in the test environment
Report of any mismatch with the signature, sample and both outputs
notes: Known intentional differences (bytecode, unsupported targets) are listed in one place and excluded explicitly, never silently
Container (.cdb) differential cases need the container parsers and run in the P5.20 gate; this issue covers the non-container grammar.
accept: Suite runs in CI and is green
Introducing a deliberate semantic change makes it fail (checked once in a test commit)

goal: Phase gate: every in-scope signature type compiles from the real databases, matches correctly and passes the differential suite, with the prefilter decision measured.
scope: Compile main and daily with the coverage report committed
Differential suite green; E2, E3, E4 and E13 results committed
Guardian starter pack compiles
Update DESIGN.md with measured figures replacing estimates
accept: All listed blockers closed with decision comments
zav scan of a raw-file corpus produces the same detections as clamscan --bytecode=no for the supported signature types

goal: A container framework that streams child objects through the same pipeline with strict, ClamAV-compatible limits, so archives and documents are scanned without materialising whole files or allowing bombs.
scope: Source union: fd range, memory slice, decompressor over a parent Source, spill file
Child sources stream in 64 KiB decompressed blocks unless they need random access
Random access: children up to 8 MiB go to a per-depth arena slab; larger ones spill to O_TMPFILE (Linux) or an unlinked temp file (macOS)
Limits: MaxScanSize, MaxFileSize, MaxRecursion 17, MaxFiles, MaxEmbeddedPE, per-member ratio guard (100:1 after 1 MiB), absolute output caps, total output budget per scan
Global big-window budget (default 64 MiB): windows over 1 MiB take a token; without one the job waits briefly, then records a limit event
Container path recorded on every result (for example archive.zip/inner.docx/word/vbaProject.bin)
notes: Spill files live in the page cache, not anonymous memory, so they do not count toward private dirty
Every limit hit is reported, and config decides whether it is a verdict
accept: Nested synthetic containers respect each limit in unit tests
Peak private dirty with the budget exhausted stays under the configured value plus the nominal figure
Container paths appear correctly in results

goal: Streaming decoders for gzip, bzip2, xz and zstd that feed the pipeline block by block and respect the big-window budget.
scope: gzip through std.compress.flate (64 KiB window), including multi-member streams
zstd through std.compress.zstd with the window capped at 8 MiB by default; larger frames raise a limit event
xz and LZMA2 through std, dictionary capped at 8 MiB by default
bzip2: our own streaming decoder (std has none), 900 KiB working set
All windows over 1 MiB take budget tokens
notes: Do not use the Home compression package: its zstd, brotli and lz4 are not the spec formats (tracked in home-lang/home)
Untrusted size fields are hints only; output is bounded by the limits, not by headers
accept: Decode conformance against reference test vectors for each format
Fuzz targets for each decoder wrapper and the bzip2 decoder run 10M iterations clean
A decompression bomb of each format stops at its limit with a limit event

goal: A zip parser that handles what real malware does to zip files: zip64, data descriptors, encryption, overlapping entries and central directories that disagree with local headers.
scope: Own parser over Source (std.zip needs a seekable File.Reader and supports store and deflate only)
Central directory first, with local-header walking as the fallback when it is missing or damaged
zip64 extra fields, data descriptors, encrypted-entry detection (reported, not decrypted)
Overlapping-entry detection (Heuristics.Zip.OverlappingFiles equivalent)
When the central directory and local headers disagree, scan both views
Methods: store, deflate, deflate64 if cheap, bzip2, lzma, zstd, xz through P5.02
notes: Members needing random access follow the P5.01 spill rules
.cdb container signatures run per member through the P4.13 hook
accept: Parses the EICAR zip files and a corpus of malformed zips without crashing
Fifield-style overlapping bombs are detected and bounded
Fuzz target runs 10M iterations clean

goal: Streaming tar (ustar, pax, GNU) and cpio support for archives that often carry Linux malware.
scope: tar through std.tar's streaming iterator, extended where pax and GNU long names need it
cpio: newc, odc and binary formats
Members stream through the pipeline with container paths
Path and size fields treated as untrusted
accept: Test vectors for each tar and cpio variant
Fuzz target clean for 10M iterations
tar.gz and tar.xz scan end to end through P5.02

goal: A PE parser that provides what signatures need: headers, sections, entry point, imports, overlay, and section hashes for .mdb and .msb.
scope: DOS and NT headers, optional header (32 and 64 bit), section table, entry point mapping to file offset
Import table and the import hash used by .imp signatures
Section hashes computed only for sections whose raw size appears in the .mdb/.msb size directory
Overlay and embedded resources exposed as child sources
Context for TDB predicates: EntryPoint, NumberOfSections
notes: Malformed PE files are common: every field access is bounds-checked and errors become limit or parse events, not crashes
accept: EP and section offsets match clamscan --debug on a PE corpus
Section-hash and import-hash signatures detect their test samples
Fuzz target clean for 10M iterations

goal: ELF and Mach-O parsers, including fat Mach-O, so Linux and macOS malware gets entry points, sections and per-slice scanning.
scope: ELF 32 and 64 bit, both endians: headers, program and section headers, entry point
Mach-O 32 and 64 bit: load commands, segments and sections, entry point (LC_MAIN and LC_UNIXTHREAD)
Fat binaries: each slice becomes a child source
Context for EP and section-relative offsets
accept: Entry points match clamscan --debug on ELF and Mach-O corpora
Fat binaries scan every slice
Fuzz targets clean for 10M iterations

goal: An HTML normaliser that produces the same stream libclamav does for target type 3, so normalised-HTML signatures fire on the same input.
scope: Byte-level state machine: lowercasing, whitespace collapse, entity decoding, comment stripping, script extraction
Outputs: the normalised stream (target 3) and extracted scripts for P5.13
MaxHTMLNormalize limit
Streaming over blocks, no whole-document buffer
notes: zig-xml is not used here: speed and ClamAV fidelity need a dedicated byte state machine
Reuse zig-waf's HTML entity tables if their semantics match; do not copy them
accept: Normalised output byte-identical to libclamav's on an HTML corpus (dumped with clamscan --leave-temps)
Fuzz target clean for 10M iterations
Throughput recorded in bench results

goal: The ASCII text normaliser for target type 7, matching libclamav's output.
scope: Lowercasing and whitespace rules as in libclamav
Applied to files classified as text
MaxScriptNormalize limit
accept: Output byte-identical to libclamav's on a text corpus
Fuzz target clean

goal: Email files are walked with zig-mime: every part decoded and scanned, target type 4 signatures applied to the message.
scope: Classify RFC 822 messages and mbox
Feed each decoded part (base64, quoted-printable) as a child source with its filename in the container path
Apply target 4 signatures to the message stream
Nested messages and multipart depth under the container limits
out_of_scope: The MIME walker itself (P2.11 to P2.15)
notes: zig-mime accepts bare LF line endings, an evasion the mail server's parser missed
accept: EICAR attached to an email is detected with the right container path
Evasion samples from zig-mime's test set are scanned
Results match clamscan on an email corpus

goal: Office Open XML documents are unpacked through the zip parser and zig-xml, with macro-enabled parts flagged and extracted.
scope: Detect docx, xlsx, pptx and their macro variants from [Content_Types].xml and relationships
Small XML parts through zig-xml (incremental mode from P2.16)
vbaProject.bin handed to the OLE2 parser as a child
External relationship targets and embedded objects recorded as findings
accept: Macro-enabled documents are flagged and their VBA reaches the OLE2 parser
A corpus of OOXML files scans without errors
Fuzz target for the OOXML layer clean

goal: OLE2 compound files and VBA macros: FAT chains, streams and MS-OVBA decompression, so macro signatures and legacy Office malware are covered.
scope: Compound file binary format: header, FAT, mini FAT, directory entries, stream reading with loop detection
VBA project streams and MS-OVBA decompression, module source exposed for target 2 signatures
Embedded objects as child sources
Limits on stream counts and sizes
notes: FAT chains in malicious files loop and overlap: detect cycles and bound reads
accept: VBA source extracted matches olevba output on a sample set
Macro signatures detect their samples
Fuzz targets clean for 10M iterations

goal: A PDF parser that finds what malicious PDFs hide: objects, streams with all common filters, object streams and embedded JavaScript.
scope: Tolerant object scanning (do not trust xref alone), plus xref and xref streams when present
Filters: FlateDecode, ASCIIHexDecode, ASCII85Decode, LZWDecode, RunLengthDecode, with chained filters and predictors
Object streams
JavaScript and embedded files extracted as child sources
Target 10 signatures applied to decoded content
out_of_scope: Encrypted PDF decryption beyond the empty user password
notes: Pathological PDFs (deep nesting, huge streams, filter loops) must stay inside the budgets: add them to the adversarial corpus
accept: JavaScript extraction works on a public malicious PDF sample set (run in the isolated environment)
Fuzz target clean for 10M iterations
Adversarial PDFs stay within time and memory bounds

goal: Normalise JavaScript extracted from HTML and PDF so obfuscated scripts match signatures written against the normalised form.
scope: Tokenizer-based normalisation compatible with libclamav: identifier renaming, string concatenation folding, whitespace and comment removal, simple unescape handling
Limits on script size and token counts
Output fed to the matching pipeline
notes: Never evaluate code; this is lexical normalisation only
accept: Normalised output matches libclamav on a script corpus
Fuzz target clean

goal: RTF documents and 7z archives with LZMA and LZMA2, two common carriers that the first format phase skipped.
scope: RTF: control word parsing, embedded objects (objdata hex) as child sources
7z: headers, encoded headers, LZMA and LZMA2 coders through std, BCJ filters
Encrypted 7z detected and reported
out_of_scope: PPMd and other rare 7z coders unless the corpus shows demand
accept: EICAR inside RTF objdata and inside 7z is detected
Fuzz targets clean for 10M iterations

goal: Heuristic detections that need no signature: entropy in risky places, executable header anomalies, content that does not match its extension, and obfuscated scripts.
